references.text: The Lord confirms that Moses will be like God to Pharaoh, and Aaron will be his prophet who speaks on his behalf.
The context where the Lord tells Moses that Aaron should speak for him, and Moses is to put the words in his mouth.
Description of a prophet who speaks God's words to the people, just as Aaron was to speak Moses' words to the people.
The Lord puts His words in the prophet's mouth, parallel to how Moses was to give words to Aaron.
People are called 'gods' (elohim) as representatives of God, just as Moses was like God to Aaron.
Jesus quotes Psalm 82:6 and explains that those who received God's word were called gods, which sheds light on the use of 'elohim' in Exodus 4:16.
Both verses illustrate the principle of divine representation where a leader acts as a spokesperson or intermediary to convey God's will or the people's needs.

Both verses are found in the same narrative flow concerning Moses' leadership and communication of God's word to the people; 4:16 gives the method (spokesperson), while 19:6 gives the content and identity.
